acronymGlossary: AFI/SAFI (Address Family Identifier / Subsequent Address Family Identifier)
IS-IS (Intermediate System to Intermediate System routing)
TACACS+ (Terminal Access Controller Access-Control System Plus)
TUN/TAP (virtual network tunnel or tap devices)
YANG (data modeling language for network config)

featureGlossary.afi/safi: BGP address family coverage. AFI selects the network family and SAFI selects the service type carried by BGP.
featureGlossary.allocation/zero-copy tuning patterns: Code patterns that reduce allocations and avoid unnecessary copies on hot paths.
featureGlossary.candidate/draft config model: A separate not-yet-active configuration tree that can be edited and checked before commit.
featureGlossary.commit confirm: A safety workflow that automatically rolls back a config change unless the operator confirms it.
featureGlossary.compile-time feature selection: Build tags, package selection, or build profiles that choose which features are compiled into an image or binary.
featureGlossary.config verify/apply/rollback model: Configuration workflow for checking a candidate config, applying it, and reverting safely when needed.
featureGlossary.control-plane hardening/sysctls: Settings that protect the control plane or tune kernel network behavior, often through sysctl values.
featureGlossary.cross-vrf route leaking: Controlled movement of routes between separate VRF routing tables.
featureGlossary.custom filter language: A project-specific policy language for matching and transforming routes.
featureGlossary.doctor/check framework: Built-in checks that diagnose host readiness, runtime problems, or configuration issues.
featureGlossary.dynamic neighbors: Ability to accept or instantiate peers from ranges, listen sockets, or discovered addresses rather than only static peer entries.
featureGlossary.external plugin sdk/api: Documented interfaces for external code to extend the product without changing the core source tree.
featureGlossary.external process integration: A mechanism for external helper processes to receive events, provide commands, or extend runtime behavior.
featureGlossary.external process policy: Route policy implemented through helper processes outside the daemon.
featureGlossary.external process protocol: A documented wire protocol used by out-of-process plugins or integrations.
featureGlossary.first release: Approximate first public release year used for context, not a quality score.
featureGlossary.generated command reference/cache: Machine-generated command documentation or command metadata used by the CLI or docs.
featureGlossary.generated composition roots: Generated startup wiring that imports or registers every component or plugin so the runtime discovers all shipped features.
featureGlossary.generated registries/schema artifacts: Generated files built from source declarations, such as plugin registries, schema imports, command caches, or feature catalogs. This row asks whether the project has machine-built wiring for features and configuration rather than only hand-maintained lists.
featureGlossary.hot reconfiguration (no restart): Changing runtime configuration without restarting the daemon or losing existing sessions.
featureGlossary.interface management model: How the project represents and applies interface configuration across Linux, VPP, or other backends.
featureGlossary.internal and external plugin process mod: Whether extensions run in-process, as child processes, or both, and how they communicate with the core.
featureGlossary.is-is route leaking: Controlled movement of routes between IS-IS Level 1 and Level 2 areas so reachability crosses the IS-IS hierarchy.
featureGlossary.language: Implementation language or runtime used by the project.
featureGlossary.license: Project license for the compared codebase.
featureGlossary.looking glass: Operator or public route visibility interface for inspecting peers, prefixes, paths, and routing decisions.
featureGlossary.machine-readable config schema: Whether automation can read a formal schema for configuration fields, types, and constraints.
featureGlossary.mcp / ai integration: Integration with the Model Context Protocol or AI assistant tooling.
featureGlossary.multipath/ecmp: Installing multiple equal-cost paths for the same destination so traffic can be load-shared.
featureGlossary.multithread model: How concurrency is structured, such as goroutines, worker threads, processes, or per-peer tasks.
featureGlossary.multithreaded: Whether the implementation can run useful routing work across multiple threads or workers.
featureGlossary.mutation testing: Tests that deliberately alter code or logic to confirm the test suite catches meaningful regressions.
featureGlossary.named copp feature: A named Control Plane Policing feature that rate-limits or filters traffic destined to the router itself.
featureGlossary.named policy definitions: Reusable named policy objects that can be attached to peers, protocols, or import and export chains.
featureGlossary.native/p4/xdp dataplane helpers: Project-owned support for programmable or accelerated dataplanes such as P4 or XDP, beyond normal Linux networking.
featureGlossary.non-systemd appliance mode: A runtime mode for appliance images that does not rely on systemd as the init or service manager.
featureGlossary.plugin architecture: Whether the project has an extension mechanism for loading or registering features outside the core.
featureGlossary.plugin-based policy: Route policy implemented by registered plugins rather than only a built-in filter language.
featureGlossary.policy-based routing: Forwarding packets according to policy rules, such as source, mark, interface, or application criteria, not only destination prefix.
featureGlossary.primary interface: Main operator or automation surface, such as CLI, HTTP API, gRPC, or SSH.
featureGlossary.protobuf/grpc api boundary: A typed API boundary defined with protobuf and exposed through gRPC.
featureGlossary.recursive next-hop: Resolving a BGP next-hop through another route before programming forwarding.
featureGlossary.rib / fib programming: Ability to install routes into an internal routing table and push forwarding entries into the kernel or dataplane.
featureGlossary.route redistribution / protocol import-e: Moving routes learned or produced by one protocol into another protocol, for example connected or static routes into BGP or IS-IS.
featureGlossary.route server and route reflector: BGP roles that redistribute routes between clients without acting like a normal transit router.
featureGlossary.route server mode: BGP route-server behavior for Internet exchange style peering, usually preserving client next-hop and policy semantics.
featureGlossary.runtime route injection: Ability to add or withdraw routes at runtime without editing static configuration and restarting.
featureGlossary.schema validation: Validation that config or API input follows the declared schema before it is applied.
featureGlossary.seed/bootstrap config database: Initial configuration storage used to bring up a fresh install or appliance image.
featureGlossary.source-owned protocol implementations: Protocol engines implemented in the project's own source tree rather than only configured through an external daemon.
featureGlossary.startup/command registration ownership: Whether each feature owns its startup hooks and commands, so removing that feature also removes its CLI, config, and runtime wiring.
featureGlossary.symptom-based diagnostics: Diagnostics organized around observed symptoms, with explanations and remediation hints.
featureGlossary.test seams and injectable components: Interfaces or constructors that let tests replace real dependencies with controlled implementations.
featureGlossary.verify/release evidence gates: Automated checks used to prove a build, release, or documentation set is coherent before publishing.
featureGlossary.vpp interface backend or vpp interface s: Whether the project can configure or target VPP-backed interfaces or exposes VPP-specific interface configuration.
featureGlossary.vrf / routing instances: Separate routing tables and interface bindings, usually used for tenant or service separation.
featureGlossary.yang-modeled config: Whether configuration is modeled with YANG or a similar schema-backed network config model.
